big: Borrowing multiplies gains and troubles. A firm with ₹200 crore of loans on ₹100 crore of equity is leaning hard on lenders. Add pledged promoter shares and a price fall can set off a chain reaction.

lines: How do I tell if a firm borrows too much?

Look at debt-to-equity, and at interest coverage: operating profit over interest. Then look at who owns the firm. High promoter holding shows commitment. Pledged shares are a warning, since lenders can sell if the price falls.

note: Promoter holding of 60% shows commitment, but quality still matters.

title: Debt and ownership
stops: A higher debt-to-equity means more borrowing
